what: THE RATCHET FOR TEXT NOBODY CAN READ, frozen 9/5/26 on build 9/5ak.
how: The eyes gate opens both surfaces at 390x844, taps the splash, waits for the game, and measures the WCAG contrast of every on-glass text box in the finished picture (the DOM says where the words are, the picture says what they look like, because a scrim drawn over the text is invisible to the styles). THE INK AND THE PAPER ARE FOUND BY SPLITTING EACH BOX AT THE MIDPOINT OF ITS OWN RANGE, not by taking the darkest and lightest tenths -- see why_it_moved below.
state: The morning card is UP, and on some captures the COLD-OPEN card is up too. MEASURED 9/6, three runs each: origin/main is stably 27 and this tree is stably 29, with the SAME ruler. The two extra are the cold-open card's own lines ('The family, the table, ten years ago.' and its WATCH button), which are present in one capture and not the other. That is a difference in WHICH CARD IS ON SCREEN at the instant of capture, not a difference in craft -- and it means the old note on this file, that the harness reaches one state deterministically, is not true. Recorded rather than smoothed over.
the_rule: This number may never go UP without the reason written here, and never silently. It is a population baseline. When a lane fixes some, lower it by hand in the same commit. gates/readable_ruler_gate.py holds the ruler itself honest: four synthetic boxes at the same 2% ink fraction that broke the old method, two nobody can read that must FAIL and two anybody can read that must PASS, so 'fix the ruler' can never quietly mean 'make the red go away'.

worst_today.note: 0 of 24 under the floor with both cards answered, measured 9/6

with_the_card_dismissed: 7 of 13 text boxes are still under the floor: the status line 1.75, OUTFIT 1.80, WHOLE MAP 2.82, BIKE 3.46, CITY 3.67, SLEEP 3.70, STANDING 4.22. So the card is not the whole story; the chips are dim on their own.
why_it_moved:
38 -> 29 on 9/6 by UI lane 11, row [eyes: faint chips]. NET DOWN NINE, AND TWO OF THE MOVE WENT UP -- both halves are written here rather than buried.

DOWN, AND MOST OF IT IS A BROKEN RULER RATHER THAN A FIX: the old method took the darkest tenth of a box against the lightest tenth, and a tenth is only 'the ink' if the ink really is a tenth of the box. The MUSIC chip is 10px text inside a 44px thumb, so the letters are TWO PER CENT of its pixels: the top tenth was still background and it scored 1.21:1 for a label anybody reads without effort. The letters are 6.17:1. OUTFIT 1.21 against 5.77. PHONE, dark text on gold, is the same error inverted: 3.24 against 6.29. AND IT FAILED THE OTHER WAY TOO, which is worse: the eight walk-pad arrows, the one control that makes the game advance, scored 4.9-5.1 and PASSED while the letters were 4.31-4.46 and did not clear the floor. WORST OF ALL IT PUNISHED THE FIX -- a bigger tap target means letters are a smaller share of the box, so the 44px thumb this lane shipped the same day made every score WORSE. On main's own pixels the ruler change alone reads 39 -> 27.

UP BY TWO, AND IT IS NOT CRAFT: with the fixed ruler main is 27 and this tree is 29, three runs each, stable both sides. The two are the cold-open card's own dim lines being present in this capture and absent in main's. Nothing was repainted to cause it and nothing is hidden by it.

REAL FIXES IN THE SAME COMMIT: the eight walk arrows and the ambient caption were genuinely under the floor and were lifted. On the screen a player actually stands on -- both cards answered, nothing on top -- it went from 7 under the floor to ZERO.
still_in_the_27: Almost all of what is left is text UNDER THE MORNING CARD'S SCRIM, which this harness holds up because it is the screen a player lands on and the only state it can reach deterministically. A modal dimming what is behind it is intended, not a craft defect. FOR EYES: the number worth ratcheting may be the one with the cards answered, where it is now ZERO -- tools/bohemia_readable_on_the_played_screen.js measures that state. That is a call for the lane that owns this harness, not a change this lane made to it.
